channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy hold as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence expect the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep the overnight rate at 2.25% at the June meeting and through 2026, despite softer Canadian data.

item.title: Euro: ECB hike seen limiting upside versus US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to deliver a one-off 25 bp ‘insurance’ hike to 2.25%, with updated projections showing higher inflation and weaker growth.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Policymakers target FX stability around fair value – ING
item.description: ING economists Peter Virovacz and Zoltán Homolya highlight that the Hungarian Forint (HUF) has sharply appreciated, with investors now treating Hungary as a quasi-eurozone economy.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause outlook after strong US jobs – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Alvin Liew notes that stronger-than-expected US payrolls and higher Oil prices have sharply reduced expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026.

item.title: Australian Dollar advances as RBA stance supports recovery ahead of key US, China data
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7070 at the time of writing on Monday, up 0.33% on the day, after touching a low near 0.7024, its weakest level in nearly two months.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed support and risk backdrop – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the US Dollar (USD) remains firm as United States (US) jobs data, higher Federal Reserve (Fed) rate expectations and rising Oil prices pressure stocks and bonds.

item.title: United Kingdom: BoE stance and Burnham politics – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s United Kingdom (UK) economists highlight political uncertainty around Andy Burnham’s potential Labour leadership challenge and its policy implications, but still expect limited radical change.

item.title: Euro: Mixed macro backdrop with weak Germany – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage flags that Euro area Sentix sentiment remains in downturn territory, with Germany still classified in recession despite modest improvement. German manufacturing orders fell sharply in April, driven by autos and machinery, even as sales showed some resilience.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Fed pricing and risk-off flows keep DXY supported – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner sees the US Dollar (USD) underpinned by hawkish Federal Reserve repricing and a risk-off tone in equities ahead of key United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) data.

item.title: Euro: Downtrend extends toward 1.1445 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that EUR/USD plunged to a three‑month low around 1.1520 after breaking several key supports.

item.title: British Pound: Growth risks and politics weigh against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad (BBH) highlights downside risks for the Pound as UK GDP is expected to contract in Q2 and markets price further Bank of England (BoE) hikes due to second-round inflation effects.

item.title: Gold steadies after hitting two-and-a-half-month low, hawkish Fed outlook caps gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) recovers some ground on Monday after sliding to its lowest level since March, as traders assess fresh geopolitical developments in the Middle East. However, hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations continue to cap the upside.

item.title: United States: Core CPI pressures stay elevated – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir expect May US CPI to show moderating but still-elevated core inflation, with core CPI seen rising 0.23% m/m and 2.8% y/y, while headline CPI is expected to climb to 4.2% y/y.

item.title: Oil: Supply risks and cautious OPEC+ hike – BNY
item.description: BNY's Bob Savage reports that Brent and WTI surged around 4–5% as Iran–Israel missile exchanges raised fears of supply disruption and higher global inflation.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Inflows and RBI support measures – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research notes that the Reserve Bank of India and government unveiled coordinated steps to attract foreign capital and support India’s external position.

item.title: Euro bounces from three-month lows at 1.1505 with all eyes on the Middle East
item.description: The Euro (EUR) turned positive against the US Dollar (USD) in the daily charts heading into the US session opening on Monday as the EUR/USD bounced to 1.1540 after hitting three-month lows at 1.1499.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises on easing geopolitical risk, RBNZ rate hike expectations
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5830 on Monday at the time of writing, up 0.62% on the day after rebounding from a two-month low touched during the Asian session.

item.title: Iran announces an end to military operations against Israel
item.description: According to Fars News, Iran's armed forces have announced an end to military operations against Israel. However, they have warned of harsher attacks if Israel resumes attacks on Lebanon. While there has been no confirmation from other media outlets.

item.title: US Dollar: Early summer rebound challenges bears – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kit Juckes notes that recent US labour data have broken the prior FX range, challenging expectations for a weaker Dollar under President Trump.

item.title: Canadian Dollar underperforms at the start of BoC policy week
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades lower against its major currency peers in the European trade on Monday amid caution surrounding the Bank of Canada’s monetary policy announcement on Wednesday.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hits over two-month low under $4,300 as US yields rally
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends losses on Monday to complete a more than 4% depreciation in the last two trading days.

item.title: Euro: ECB hikes seen as growth headwind – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad (BBH) anticipates the European Central Bank (ECB) will end its pause with a 25 bps hike to 2.25% as core and services inflation run above forecasts.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Shorts jump despite recession – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Molly Schwartz and Jane Foley report that Canadian Dollar (CAD) net short positions have surged about 36% to their highest level since December 2025.

item.title: US President Trump expresses both Iran and Israel looking for ceasefire
item.description: In the European trading session, United States (US) President Donald Trump has expressed confidence that both Israel and Iran are looking for a ceasefire, through a post on Truth Social, while maintaining the stance that the US blockade on Iranian seaports will remain intact until a final deal with

item.title: Indian Rupee plummets as renewed Middle East conflicts boost oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) starts the week on a negative note against the US Dollar (USD), with the USD/INR pair jumping to near 95.65.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: At two-month highs, with 0.8000 in focus
item.description: The US Dollar is rallying for the second consecutive day against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Monday, reaching levels near 0.8000 for the first time in the last two months.

item.title: US President Trump urges Israel and Iran to pause attacks immediately
item.description: United States (US) President Donald urges Iran and Israel to pause the exchange of attacks, through a post on Truth Social, during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: British Pound: Seen lower against Euro and US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner expects the Bank of England (BoE) to avoid tightening this year, with only modest rate hikes priced by markets.

item.title: Euro edges lower vs Japanese Yen as BoJ tightening bets support JPY
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.10 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.32% on the day, as the Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to benefit from a favorable backdrop driven by expectations of higher interest rates in Japan and renewed warnings from Japanese authorities regarding currency weakness.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Inflow tools preferred over hikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay highlights that the Reserve Bank of India kept its policy rate at 5.25% and signalled a preference to bolster the Rupee via capital inflow measures rather than tightening.
